timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hey, what's up you guys? Welcome back to my channel. My name is Coach Coco and I love
volleyball. So much so my channel's filled with tips, tricks, hacks and anything you could
ever need to know about volleyball. So today I thought I would make a different kind of
video showing you all the different types of volleyball serves. And in this video I'm
going to highlight some serves that are really popular throughout the junior level, the
high school level and the collegiate level so that way you can get a better idea of exactly
what you need to practice on and what these different types of serves look like. I'm
also going to tell you how effective they are and how often you should be practicing
serves with that. Let's get right into it. Now first let's do these overhand serve and
this is arguably the most popular. Now with the overhand serve, a lot of you guys are working
on that but there are some different types of overhand serves. There's a standing overhand,
standing float and standing topspin. So there's not just one general overhand serve. It's
also too important to remember that the overhand serve is the standard serve in many standard
volleyball games. So a lot of you guys if you're doing the underhand I suggest you start
moving towards the overhand because you can't really do underhand when you get to a certain
level. Also I also want you to note that many players start working on their overhand
serve almost immediately after learning how to play. That's because sometimes it can
take a while and I want you to be able to have enough time to go ahead and perfect it.
And some of the common struggles with the overhand is to not get it all the way over
the net. I know that's frustrating. However there's a way to fix that with proper form.
That means that bow, that arrow, making sure you have the form to be able to serve over
the net. Also if you want to play volleyball I suggest you start working on it immediately
as soon as you know you want to play. I do not count the underhand serve as a serve because
it's more for recreational purposes. However some teams allow you to underhand serve but
please don't bet on that information. If you can learn your overhand working your overhand
because sometimes it takes some time to get it. Either there's players who can't get
over or players who serve too hard but work at that. So I have a great tutorial on my
channel about the overhand serve as well as a standing float. So I'm going to tag those
in the description below so go ahead and check those out if you want to start working
on your overhand serve.
Now here's something I get comments on a lot which is the jump serve. The jump serve is
very popular and men's volleyball and at the collegiate level. But here's some things
about the jump serve you might not know. Sometimes the jump serve can be unpredictable. It's
one of those serves that you really have to practice as it really mocks a back real
attack. It's really cool looking and it's kind of hard to receive. However there's a
serve that is harder to receive. Unless you practice this there's a high trajectory
it's going out. Please practice a serve if you're considering doing this. This is an advanced
serve. You need to know all your other serves before this.
Alright you all now here's my favorite serve which is the jump float. This is the most
popular that I've seen in the last couple of years. The jump float has really easy steps.
It kind of mocks a standing serve with some additional steps. However it is very hard
to receive the jump float. That's because it comes kind of straight over the net and
if you're receiving the ball and serve receive sometimes that ball can arguably move in
the air. I'm not joking it can move in the air. Now if you overpower the serve it's going
to coast right out of bounds. So make sure if you're learning how to do your jump float
or your standing float you understand the depth of the court so you're not just hitting
the ball straight towards the wall like I did when I first started playing. This is my
favorite serve because it's easy effective and powerful in a game and it's hard to read.
That is what we want. We want something that is hard to read. Once you've learned your
overhand serve, your float, your top spin then start working on your jump float because
it is going to take you a long way especially when you start playing up with higher level,
volleyball teams and higher level volleyball games. And it's something that you can put
in your pocket. What kind of serve do you like to do? Put that in the comments below.

I will see you guys next time.
